title: Reported speech
subtitle: Tense and modal changes, reported questions, reporting verbs

theory.title: Reported speech: tense and modal changes

blocks.text: We use reported speech when we want to say what someone else said. If the reporting verb is in the past, we usually have to change the tense of what the person actually said.

rows.question: Tim said he **needed** a credit card.
Tim said he **was taking** Lizzie shopping.
Tim said he'd **bought** Tom a present.

rows.statement: I've **been thinking** about buying a car.
rows.question: Tim said he'd **been thinking** about buying a car.
Tim said he'd **spent** six euros.

rows.statement: I **was hoping** to find a new top.
rows.question: Tim said he'd **been hoping** to find a new top.

rows.statement: I'd **looked** everywhere for my credit card.
rows.question: Tim said he'd **looked** everywhere for his credit card before he found it.

rows.statement: I'd **been looking** for that book for weeks.
rows.question: Tim said he'd **been looking** for that book for weeks before he found it.
Tim said he **was going to** go shopping.
Tim said he **would need** a credit card.
Tim said he **could take** Lizzie shopping.

rows.statement: I **must / have to** go to the supermarket.
rows.question: Tim said he **had to** go to the supermarket.
Tim said he **might go** shopping later.

blocks.text: We do not need to make any changes to the verb tense or modal when we are reporting a scientific fact or when something is still true.
blocks.note: 'Most banks **charge** interest,' said Tim. → Tim said most banks **charge** interest.

theory.title: Reported speech: pronoun and determiner changes

blocks.text: With reported speech, we also usually have to change some pronouns and determiners.

rows.question: Tim said he had lost **his** credit card.
Tim said he loved **the / that** sweater.
Tim said **it** was a lovely sweater.
Tim said he loved **the / those** sweaters.
Tim said **they** were lovely sweaters.
Tim said he was going to buy **them**.

theory.title: Reported speech: time and place changes

blocks.text: With reported speech, we also usually have to change words and phrases connected to time and place.

rows.question: Tim said he usually shopped **there**.
Tim said he was shopping **then / at that moment**.
Tim said he was going shopping **the next / following day**.
Tim said he was going shopping **that night**.
Tim said he was going shopping **the following week**.

rows.negative: the day before / the previous day
rows.question: Tim said he'd been shopping **the day before / the previous day**.

rows.negative: the week / month / year before · the previous week / month / year
rows.question: Tim said he'd been shopping **the week before / the previous week**.
Tim said he'd been shopping two days **before / previously**.

blocks.text: We do not need to make any changes to time words / phrases when the information is still true at the moment of speaking / writing.
blocks.note: 'I'm going shopping **tomorrow**,' said Tim to Ben. → Ben immediately called Lizzie and said, 'Tim said he's going shopping **tomorrow**.'

blocks.text: We use reported questions when we want to say what someone else asked. We use the same rules regarding tense, pronoun and time and place word / phrase changes as we do with reported speech.

rows.use: have, do, be or modal (yes / no questions) → if / whether
rows.example: 'Can you get me an ice cream, Tom?' asked Tim. → Tim asked Tom **if / whether** he could get him an ice cream.

rows.use: what, who, which, when, where, why and how stay the same
rows.example: 'Why did you buy these shoes?' asked Tim. → Tim asked me **why I had bought** those shoes.

blocks.text: In direct questions we use the question form and question marks (**Can you …?**). In reported questions we don't use the question form or question marks (**asked if he could …**).
Different reporting verbs take different grammatical patterns. Some verbs can take more than one pattern.

exercises.title: A · Correct form of the verb
exercises.instruction: Complete using the correct form of the verb in brackets.

items.prompt: Stewart said he ___ (not / want) any dessert as he was full.
Derek said that he and Belinda ___ (see) Adam recently.
When I called, Susie said she ___ (give) the dog a bath so she asked me to phone back in half an hour.
Marcus said he ___ (try) to find a flat for ages before he finally found one he liked.
Debbie says she ___ (decide) to quit her job but I don't believe her.
Our English teacher said that Shakespeare ___ (be) probably the greatest writer in the English language ever.
Richard said he and Patricia ___ (be going to) invite her parents for the weekend, but I don't know if they went or not.
Charlotte said last night that she really ___ (love) me, even if she doesn't always show it.
Ollie said to Linda that he ___ (ask) me to be his best man on Monday but in fact he asked Grant.
Pete told Francis he ___ (bring up) by his grandparents but in fact he hadn't at all.

exercises.title: B · Tick if correct, or rewrite
exercises.instruction: If the word or phrase in bold is correct, rewrite it as it is. If it is incorrect, rewrite it correctly.

items.prompt: On Monday, my boss said I **can take** Wednesday off, but he changed his mind today for some reason.
The receptionist said that if I wanted to have breakfast, I **will** have to pay extra.
A lot of people at school have said that Andrew **may** get the lead in the school play.
Colin said he'd **been planning** to ask Rich to move in with him for ages.
Lucy says she **would** let us know as soon as she gets the tickets.
Jordan said that she **has to** get up at five thirty every morning.
Before he got his results, Philip said that he **may** have to retake some exams, but now he knows he doesn't have to.
Did Mrs Morgan say why **she'd called**?
Paul said he **should** be here tomorrow night at about nine.
Dan said he **must drive** to Liverpool that night, but apparently he didn't go in the end.

items.prompt: Tonya said ___ TV was broken and asked if she could come around to watch the football with us.

exercises.title: D · Key word transformation
exercises.instruction: Complete each second sentence using the word given, so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence. Write between two and five words in each gap.

items.prompt:

Jerry said that ___ be travelling round Europe.

'I had Evan and Christie over for dinner last night,' said Liz. **before**
Liz said she ___ had Evan and Christie over for dinner.

'Daz came here two days ago and then suddenly left,' said Barry. **gone**
Barry said that Daz had ___ and then suddenly left.

'We're going on our yearly diet tomorrow,' said Jessie and Sandy. **starting**
Jessie and Sandy said together that they ___ yearly diet the next day.

'I can pick you two boys up from school this afternoon,' said their father to George and Kevin. **that**
George and Kevin's father told his sons ___ up from school that afternoon.

'I'll buy these as they're so cheap!' said Toby. **going**
Toby said he ___ as they were so cheap.

'You must study harder, Dave,' said Dave's mum. **him**
Dave's mum ___ study harder.

'I think you may be coming down with flu,' Greg said to me. **thought**

'I don't know why they haven't contacted me recently,' said Tine. **been**
Tine said she didn't know why ___ recently.

'Everything was different yesterday,' said Ben. **been**
Ben said everything ___ before.

exercises.title: F · Rewrite as reported questions
exercises.instruction: Rewrite as reported questions, beginning with the words given.

items.prompt:
'Have you had your ear pierced?'
**My mum asked me if**
acceptedAnswers: My mum asked me if I had had my ear pierced.
My mum asked me if I'd had my ear pierced.

items.prompt:
'Can I meet you there at six o'clock tonight, Doug?'
**Julian wanted to know whether**
acceptedAnswers: Julian wanted to know whether he could meet Doug there at six o'clock that night.
Julian wanted to know whether he could meet him there at six o'clock that night.

items.prompt:
'Are you still moving to Blackpool next week?'
**Fiona asked Rod and Jenny whether**
acceptedAnswers: Fiona asked Rod and Jenny whether they were still moving to Blackpool the following week.
Fiona asked Rod and Jenny whether they were still moving to Blackpool the next week.

items.prompt:
'Does Graham have to wear a suit to work?'
**I asked Mrs Daley if Graham**
acceptedAnswers: I asked Mrs Daley if Graham had to wear a suit to work.
I asked Mrs Daley if Graham had to wear a suit to work

items.prompt:
'Do you want someone to feed your cat while you're away?'
**Jan asked me if**
acceptedAnswers: Jan asked me if I wanted someone to feed my cat while I was away.
Jan asked me if I wanted someone to feed my cat while I was away

items.prompt:
'Can you guess what I've given Lindsay for her birthday?'
**Daisy asked Wendy if**
acceptedAnswers: Daisy asked Wendy if she could guess what she had given Lindsay for her birthday.
Daisy asked Wendy if she could guess what she'd given Lindsay for her birthday.

items.prompt:
'Do you love me or not, Gloria?'
**Fred asked Gloria whether**
acceptedAnswers: Fred asked Gloria whether she loved him or not.
Fred asked Gloria whether she loved him or not

items.prompt:
'Will Simon be coming to the party tomorrow night?'
**Adrian wondered whether**
acceptedAnswers: Adrian wondered whether Simon would be coming to the party the following night.
Adrian wondered whether Simon would be coming to the party the next night.

items.prompt:
'Tell me if you were anywhere near 34 Aylesford Street last night!'
**The police officer demanded to know whether**
acceptedAnswers: The police officer demanded to know whether Sykes had been anywhere near 34 Aylesford Street the night before.
The police officer demanded to know whether I had been anywhere near 34 Aylesford Street the night before.

items.prompt: She asked me why I was thinking of quitting the gym.
acceptedAnswers: Why are you thinking of quitting the gym?
Why are you thinking of quitting the gym?

items.prompt: He asked her what the difference was between a refugee and an asylum seeker.
acceptedAnswers: What is the difference between a refugee and an asylum seeker?
What's the difference between a refugee and an asylum seeker?

items.prompt: They asked us how we had got on with Peter three days before.
acceptedAnswers: How did you get on with Peter three days ago?
How have you got on with Peter in the last three days?

items.prompt: I asked them when they had last been on holiday.
acceptedAnswers: When were you last on holiday?
When did you last go on holiday?

items.prompt: She asked him which of them he preferred.
acceptedAnswers: Which of them do you prefer?
Which of them do you prefer?

items.prompt: I asked you how you were going to get to Manchester tomorrow.
acceptedAnswers: How are you going to get to Manchester tomorrow?
How are you going to get to Manchester tomorrow?

items.prompt: Carl asked Megan who she had been out with the weekend before.
acceptedAnswers: Who were you out with last weekend?
Who did you go out with last weekend?

items.prompt: Megan asked Carl what gave him the right to ask questions like that.
acceptedAnswers: What gives you the right to ask questions like that?
What gives you the right to ask questions like that?
